newsitem.title: FINLAND: TAMROCK SEES IMPROVING PROFITS IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: TAMROCK SEES IMPROVING PROFITS IN 1997.

text.p: Finnish mining equipment group Tamrock Oy said on Monday it expected full-year profit before extras and tax to improve on last year's 141 million markka and net profit to improve clearly thanks to extraordinary gains.
"The 1997 result before extraordinary items, voluntary reserves and taxes is expected to improve on 1996," Tamrock said in a statement with its January-June results.
"The net result is estimated to show a clear improvement on last year, principally as a result of extraordinary income," it said.
In 1996, net profit was 65 million markka.
At end-June, Tamrock's orderbook at 1.2 billion markka was some 50 percent higher than one year earlier, the company said.
"Tamrock has a clearly higher orderbook than a year ago, due mainly to the VAB acquisition," it said, referring to Austrian Voest-Alpine Bergtechnik (VAB) bought in September 1996.

"The market outlook still continues to be generally positive, but uncertainty has increased as a result of the steep decline of the gold price, especially in the main gold mining areas of North America, Africa and Australia," Tamrock said. @
"Demand for construction equipment is expected to remain at the present level or even to increase," it said.
Tamrock's first-half net sales were 2.50 billion markka and comparable net sales rose seven percent on the corresponding period last year.
The group's January-June profit before extraordinary items and tax rose 18 percent year-on-year to 110 million markka.
